subject.title: Feature: Respect userTimezone in memory file timestamps and naming

question: Should bundled session-memory artifacts use `agents.defaults.userTimezone` instead of the gateway host timezone for filename date, fallback HHMM slug, and `# Session` header?
rationale: Current docs and shipped behavior say session-memory uses host local dates, while memory-core auto-flush already uses configured user timezone; choosing the permanent artifact contract affects upgrade compatibility and config scope.

options.title: Extend userTimezone to session-memory
options.body: Implement the narrow behavior change with existing configured-timezone helpers and update session-memory tests/docs, accepting the filename/header shift for host/user timezone mismatches.

options.title: Keep host-local session-memory
options.body: Close or reframe the request and keep docs explicit that session-memory artifacts follow the gateway host timezone while auto-flush uses configured user timezone.

options.title: Add a memory-specific timezone knob
options.body: Introduce a dedicated setting only if maintainers want memory artifacts decoupled from both host-local and `userTimezone`, with schema/docs/upgrade proof.

recommendation.title: Extend userTimezone to session-memory
recommendation.body: Implement the narrow behavior change with existing configured-timezone helpers and update session-memory tests/docs, accepting the filename/header shift for host/user timezone mismatches.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a config/product contract decision across memory-core and session-memory surfaces, and this owner has recent history on the relevant time/memory paths.
